title: Add Terraform modules for health-check based routing + DNS primitives for automated regional failover
author: Victor Alvarez
description:
Context: Regional failover automation upgrade needs consistent, auditable DNS/edge primitives to support health-check based routing. Historically we’ve had per-env hand-rolled Route53 records and ad-hoc health checks, which makes controlled failover tests risky and rollback/error-prone.

This PR introduces a small set of Terraform modules used by the failover orchestrator and/or runbook-driven mitigations:
- modules/route53_healthcheck: standard HTTP(s) health checks (with optional SNI, expected status codes, and failure thresholds)
- modules/weighted_failover_records: creates weighted A/AAAA records across regions, with optional health check association per target
- modules/failover_guardrails: environment-specific safeguards (prod-only protections) implemented via variable validation + Terraform preconditions

Key behaviors:
- Supports progressive failover by allowing weights to be set per region (e.g. us-east-1=95, us-west-2=5) and by exposing a consistent output schema consumed by routing automation.
- Guardrails for prod:
  - require explicit enable_prod_changes=true (default false) to apply record changes in prod workspaces
  - enforce minimum TTL (>= 30s) and maximum TTL (<= 300s) for records managed by these modules
  - optional allowlist of record names for prod to prevent accidental creation/renames outside the approved set
  - optional “change_window_id” annotation (string) that is required in prod to tie DNS changes to the planned game day / change window (used as a tag)
- Adds an examples/failover-routing/ example showing how to wire a service endpoint (api.<env>.redwood.ai) to regional targets and health checks.

Out of scope:
- No changes to the orchestrator or trigger engine here; this is just the Terraform layer for the routing/DNS primitives.

Testing:
- terraform validate + fmt
- tflint (module and example)
- plan-only for staging workspace to verify no drift outside intended records

Rollout notes:
- The guardrails intentionally block prod applies unless enable_prod_changes=true is set and record_name is in allowlist (if provided). This is to reduce the chance of accidental record edits during early game days.

Refs:
- Linear ENG-2849 (Terraform automation for routing/DNS primitives)
- Project: Regional failover automation upgrade (SRE + Smart Routing)
- Related: DNS TTL strategy thread / change window expectations (Release Eng + Infra Networking)
commits: modules: add route53_healthcheck module with standard defaults + validation
modules: add weighted_failover_records for regional targets (A/AAAA) w/ health check association
guardrails: prod protections via variable validation + lifecycle preconditions
examples: add failover-routing example for api endpoint + regional targets
docs: module READMEs + usage notes (TTL, allowlist, change window tags)
ci: add tflint to module checks and fix lint issues in examples
conversation:
Irene Choi (review): Guardrails look good. Can we enforce TTL bounds only for records created by this module? I don’t want to block other zones that have >300s TTL for non-failover records.
Victor Alvarez (author): Yep — TTL validation is scoped to this module’s ttl var only (not global). Updated README to call out that these modules should only manage failover-related records. Also tightened variable names to avoid reuse in unrelated modules.

Emily Zhao (review): For health checks: are we pinning the path and expected codes? We’ve seen false positives when an upstream returns 200 with an error payload.
Victor Alvarez (author): Default is /healthz and expected_codes="200". Added variables for path + matcher so services can opt into 204, etc. I avoided payload matching because Route53 health checks can’t validate body, but we can point checks at the dedicated synthetic endpoint that already fails closed. Added that guidance to README.

Connor O'Brien (review): Prod safety: I like enable_prod_changes. Please make sure default is false and that plans clearly show the reason it’s failing (precondition message). Also request tagging with change window.
Victor Alvarez (author): Done. Added a precondition with an explicit error message: "prod applies blocked unless enable_prod_changes=true and change_window_id is set". change_window_id is now required in prod (workspace check). Tags include failover=true, owner=infra-networking, and change_window_id.

Miles Thornton (review): Progressive failover requires weights, but also a way to ‘zero’ a region quickly. Are we allowing a target weight of 0?
Victor Alvarez (author): Yes — module accepts 0..100. Validation ensures sum(weights) > 0 and each entry is within bounds. Added an example for canary 1% and for hard drain (0%).

Benji Okafor (review): Please add an allowlist option for prod record names. We’ve had accidental renames cause outage-level incidents.
Victor Alvarez (author): Added record_name_allowlist (list) and a precondition that record_name must be in allowlist when workspace=prod and allowlist is non-empty. Also added outputs to make record_name explicit for downstream auditing.

Irene Choi (follow-up): Can we avoid creating/destroying health checks during weight-only changes? Health check IDs changing makes audit trails messy.
Victor Alvarez (author): Health checks are separate resources in route53_healthcheck module. In the example I now create checks once per region and pass IDs into weighted_failover_records. Weight changes will not touch health checks.

System (CI): tflint failed on examples/failover-routing (unused variable, missing required_version)
Victor Alvarez (author): Fixed. Added required_version (>= 1.5.0) and removed unused var. Re-ran CI.

Irene Choi (approval): Approved. Please coordinate actual prod enablement with Release Eng and keep enable_prod_changes default false.
Connor O'Brien (approval): Approved with note: ensure change window ID is included for game day applies.
Emily Zhao (approval): Approved.
release_notes: Infra/Terraform: added standard modules for Route53 health checks and weighted regional DNS records to support automated/progressive regional failover, with prod-only guardrails (explicit enable flag, TTL bounds, optional record allowlist, change window tagging).
